**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Banana fruit (fingers/pods) — specifically the distal/blossom ends (tips)
- **Key features**:
  - Dark brown to black, dry, shriveled rot confined to the tip (blossom end) of each banana finger
  - The necrotic tissue appears desiccated, mummified, and dark — visually resembling the ash end of a cigar
  - The rest of the banana skin is yellow/green and relatively intact
  - Small scattered dark flecks on the fruit surface
  - Multiple fingers on the bunch are uniformly affected at the tip

**Differential reasoning:**

| Class | Fit |
|---|---|
| **Cigar_End_Rot** | **Exact match** — dry, dark brown-black necrosis starting at blossom end, "cigar ash" appearance |
| Anthracnose | Produces sunken, dark water-soaked lesions spreading over skin surface, not tip-confined |
| Bunchy_Top | Leaf/plant architecture disease (narrow bunched leaves, streaks); not fruit tip rot |
| Cordana_Leaf_Spot | Leaf disease with oval brown spots — not fruit |
| Panama_Disease | Vascular wilt — affects pseudostem/rhizome with internal browning, not fruit tips |
| Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka | Leaf streak/spot diseases — not fruit |

The defining hallmark here is the **dry, mummified, dark tip rot restricted to the blossom end** of banana fingers — the textbook presentation of Cigar End Rot (caused by *Trachysphaera fructigena* or *Verticillium theobromae*).
